catalog_quote: Si bien entre las diversas fuentes de datos se dan algunas contradicciones y vacilaciones, el acento en cacaopera obviamente no tenía una posición fija y, en consecuencia, era distintivo. Los siguientes ejemplos demuestran el carácter libre de la colocación de este suprasegmental: ... Cam. álu 'perro' ... Cam. asá 'gavilán' ... Cam. kisú 'armadillo' ... Cam. yúsu 'camarón' ... Cam. sárra 'olla' ... Cam. urrá 'jocote' ... Cam. íkiri 'chacalín (un tipo de camarón)' ... Cam. inkiná 'guineo' ... Cam. indúrra 'tortilla' ... audit.reasoning: (1) Quote confirmed verbatim in the held Bertoglia 1989 text layer at journal p.119, sec. 3.3, exactly as the locator says; sec. 2.3 (p.118) and the vowel-length remark (p.123) also present. (2) The deciding source is the only dedicated phonology of this extinct language (Glottolog's 4 refs reduce to this article, its parent thesis, and Brinton's 1895 sketch, which says nothing about accent); it is a 1989 structural analysis pooling every extant dataset, and no later or instrumental study exists or can exist. Constenla 1987, fetched sources now from the UCR open archive, is silent on Cacaopera accent and only cautions that suprasegmental transcription in Misumalpan sources is unreliable, a caveat Bertoglia herself makes ('contradicciones y vacilaciones') and the record already carries in exq_. (3) The one genuinely useful unheld item is Campbell 1975 (paywalled JSTOR), the primary data behind Be

sources.quote: No statement on Cacaopera accent; gives segmental inventory only and warns that the Misumalpan sources transcribe suprasegmentals unreliably. Notes Cacaopera corpus is <=~500 lexical items (Lehmann 1920:604-623 and Campbell 1975:146-153 the only sources).
